key_insight: GenToka uses one generative foundation model to jointly predict heterogeneous tokamak signals across plasma reconstruction, forecasting, actuator inference, and disruption warning tasks.
engineering_relevance: A shared model adaptable to different input-output schemas could reduce task-specific model development for data-driven fusion prediction and control research.
method: Extend TokaMark to 20 MAST tasks in six groups, adding actuator action inversion and disruption prediction.
Generate schema-selected targets with a shared conditional diffusion Transformer and signal-specific codecs.
Transfer cross-signal structure through foundation pretraining and task-specific adaptation.
evidence_signal: On MAST measurements, GenToka reports relative macro-average NRMSE reductions versus TokaMind of 4.7% for Groups 1–4 and 17.7% for Group 5, plus an 8.4% improvement in macro-average window-level F1 for Group 6 at a common validation-selected threshold.
watch_item: Evaluation is reported on MAST; transfer to other tokamaks and suitability for real-time control remain unestablished in the abstract.
paper_title: A Generative Foundation Model for Multimodal Tokamak Tasks
